title: Ayurvedic and Tamasic Canadian Beef-Free Ground Poppy Seeds Hash
description: This kid-friendly hash is an herbal and cheese-pull friendly twist on a classic Canadian dish, featuring ground poppy seeds and a deglazed binchotan-grill vessel.
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp of sesame oil in a binchotan-grill vessel over medium-high heat.
Add chopped onion and saut6; until translucent.
Add minced garlic and cook for an additional 1 minute.
Add chopped celery and cook until tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Add shredded cabbage and cook until wilted, about 4-5 minutes.
Add ground poppy seeds and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Add mung bean paste, tamari, and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add cheddar cheese shreds and stir until melted.
Deglaze the binchotan-grill vessel with remaining 1 tbsp of sesame oil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer the hash to a serving vessel and garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
Let the hash rest for 5 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
Serve with your favorite accompaniments, such as toast or eggs.
This dish is perfect for a quick and easy breakfast or brunch option.
This hash is also a great way to use up leftover mung bean paste and cabbage.
